note: Viable operating envelope for the GA100 direct-die on a water cold plate, measured 26 Aug 2026 to re-centre the accelerator arm of the catalogue. The old sweep points (400 W and 700 W on 88 CFM air) are far past the cliff and return nothing but RUNAWAY.

result.comment: The GA100 has no steady state above ~250 W on this cold plate. A real H100 runs at 700 W, so the model is a long way from the part -- that gap is a finding to chase, not something to configure around.

what_was_ruled_out: Package: the OLD lidded skylake stack runs away at 400 W too.
The spreading correction: runs away with and without --spreading.
Cooling class: water at 0.0549 K/W -- half the air boundary -- still runs away at 400 W.
Leakage fraction: still runs away at 0.10, against the assumed 0.25.
what_remains: The cause established so far is commit 0f91991 (20 Aug), which made leakage feedback live on the accelerator after 43 studies had been constant-power solves -- see accelerator_runaway_cause.json. What is NOT yet established is why the coupled solve is this steep: none of the four levers above moves the cliff, which points at the GA100 power map itself (MEMCTRL_B0 sets the peak at 1.47 W/mm^2 on an 8.3 mm^2 block, from an ASSUMED class split) rather than at the cooling. That is the next thing to test.
pump_power_caveat: The flow solver bottoms out at 1e-05 m^3/s and reports 0 W of pump power with "face velocity 0.02 m/s below the plausible water range". That flow is right per device -- the LCEstimator CDU is 0.02 m^3/s across ~1950 devices, i.e. 1.0e-05 each -- so the implausibility is the COLD PLATE GEOMETRY, not the flow. CoolingSpec sizes a finned base for the die; a real GPU cold plate is microchannel. Capturing honest pump power needs the microchannel geometry from docs/chip_design_lit/design_physics/.
SUPERSEDED: 26 Aug 2026 by microchannel_coldplate.json. The cliff measured here is a property of the FINNED WATER BLOCK this run used, not of the GA100. On a direct-die microchannel cold plate the same die runs 64 C at 700 W. The measurements below stand; the conclusion drawn from them does not.
